pqac-8d739a1d: The excerpt only provides qualitative results, not the exact numerical biomass yields, nutrient uptake values, or detailed statistical comparisons by site and year. It states that Pennisetum glaucum and Urochloa brizantha cv. Marandu produced the highest biomass on a 3-year average, with P. glaucum producing 210% more biomass than other cover crops at one site. Question: What were the exact biomass yields, nutrient uptake values, and statistical differences among cover crops at each site and year?

I cannot answer. The provided context does not include the exact biomass yields, nutrient uptake values, or statistical differences among cover crops at each site and year. It only reports qualitative patterns: *Pennisetum glaucum* and *Urochloa brizantha* cv. Marandu had the highest 3-year average biomass, with *P. glaucum* producing 210% more biomass than other cover crops at one site; tropical grasses and the cover-crop mixture had intermediate biomass at that high-biomass site; *Crotalaria spectabilis* decomposed rapidly and released more nutrients, especially nitrogen; and the mixture supported higher soybean populations and yields.
